notes.Types of tourism & reasons to travel:
## Overview
People travel for different reasons. Tourism is classified by purpose and by where people travel.
## Key ideas
- Leisure, business (MICE), visiting friends and relatives (VFR), health, religious, educational, adventure, eco-tourism.
- Domestic, inbound, outbound tourism.
- Day visitors vs tourists (at least one night).
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Inbound tourism | Visitors arriving from another country |
| Outbound tourism | Residents travelling abroad |
| MICE | Meetings, incentives, conferences, exhibitions |
## Formulas and facts
- A tourist stays away from home for at least one night but less than a year.
## Worked example
**Classify a German couple diving in the Maldives.**
**Answer:** Inbound leisure (adventure) tourism.
## More detail
### Types of tourism
| Type | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Domestic | Within your own country | Malé family visiting a guesthouse in Maafushi |
| Inbound | Visitors entering a country | Chinese tourists arriving in the Maldives |
| Outbound | Residents travelling abroad | Maldivians going to Sri Lanka for shopping |
| Leisure | Holidays, relaxation | Resort stay |
| Business / MICE | Meetings, incentives, conferences, exhibitions | Tourism fair in Malé |
| VFR | Visiting friends and relatives | Students returning from abroad |
| Special interest | Diving, surfing, wellness, religious, medical, educational | Hajj, surf trips |
- **Day visitor (excursionist)**: does not stay overnight. **Tourist**: stays at least one night, less than a year.
### Factors that encourage travel
- More disposable income and paid holidays, cheaper flights, online booking, better transport, easier visas (visa on arrival), social media influence.
### Exam-style question
**Q: Explain two reasons why business tourism is important to a destination. (4)** Business tourists spend more per day (hotels, meals, transport); they travel all year, reducing seasonality.
## Common mistakes
- Mixing up inbound and outbound.
## Exam tips
- Always say from whose country's point of view.
notes.Sustainable tourism:
## Overview
Sustainable tourism meets today's needs without harming future generations.
## Key ideas
- Three pillars: economic, social/cultural, environmental.
- Examples: solar power, reef protection rules, local employment, waste recycling.
- Carrying capacity and visitor management.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Sustainable tourism | Tourism that protects the environment and benefits locals long term |
| Carrying capacity | Maximum visitors without damage |
| Eco-tourism | Responsible travel to natural areas |
## Formulas and facts
- Codes of conduct educate tourists.
## Worked example
**Give one way a resort can be more sustainable.**
**Answer:** Use solar power to reduce diesel use.
## More detail
- **Sustainable tourism** balances economic, environmental and socio-cultural needs now and for the future.
- **Ecotourism**: small-scale, nature-based, educates visitors and benefits local people.
### Sustainable practices in the Maldives
- Solar panels and energy-saving systems on resorts; reef-safe sunscreen; no single-use plastics.
- Marine protected areas (e.g. Hanifaru Bay biosphere reserve); limits on numbers when swimming with manta rays and whale sharks.
- Local employment and training; buying fish and produce from local islands.
- Green tax charged to tourists funds environmental projects.
### Responsible tourist behaviour
- Do not touch or stand on coral; take litter home; respect local dress codes on inhabited islands; use registered guides.
### Exam-style question
**Q: Evaluate the use of entry fees at a marine protected area. (6)** Raises funds for conservation and limits crowding; but may discourage budget visitors and needs staff to enforce. Conclude whether benefits outweigh the costs.
## Common mistakes
- Only mentioning the environment.
## Exam tips
- Explain how the action helps, not just what it is.
notes.Types of tourists & destinations:
## Overview
Tourists have different needs, and destinations attract different visitors.
## Key ideas
- Customer types: families, couples, groups, business travellers, people with special needs.
- Destination types: coastal, island, mountain, city, rural, purpose-built.
- Matching products and services to customer needs.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Special needs | Needs such as wheelchair access or dietary requirements |
| Purpose-built destination | Created mainly for tourism |
## Formulas and facts
- Island resorts suit couples (honeymoon) and divers.
## Worked example
**Suggest two facilities a family needs at a resort.**
**Answer:** Kids' club and family rooms.
## More detail
### Customer types and their needs
| Customer type | Typical needs |
|---|---|
| Families with young children | Kids' club, family rooms, safe beaches, child menus |
| Couples / honeymooners | Privacy, romantic dining, spa, overwater villas |
| Business travellers | Wi-Fi, meeting rooms, fast check-in, airport transfer |
| Backpackers | Cheap guesthouses, local transport, social atmosphere |
| Groups | Group discounts, group activities, large tables |
| Older travellers | Accessibility, medical facilities, slower pace |
| Visitors with disabilities | Ramps, accessible rooms, trained staff |
### Types of destination
- Coastal and island, city, rural, mountain, heritage and cultural, purpose-built resorts, cruise destinations.
- **Gateway**: main point of entry (Velana International Airport).
### Exam-style question
**Q: Explain how a resort could meet the needs of a family with a baby. (4)** Provide a cot and baby-sitting service, child-safe pool area, baby food on menus, and family-friendly activities.
## Common mistakes
- Giving general facilities not linked to the customer.
## Exam tips
- Match each facility to a need.
notes.Global tourism:
## Overview
Global tourism has grown due to changes in transport, technology and incomes.
## Key ideas
- Growth factors: cheaper flights, more leisure time, higher incomes, internet booking.
- Major tourist regions and flows; factors affecting demand (safety, exchange rates, events).
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Disposable income | Money left after essentials |
| Low-cost airline | Airline with cheap, basic fares |
## Formulas and facts
- Crises such as pandemics reduce global arrivals.
## Worked example
**Explain one reason for growth in international tourism.**
1. Low-cost airlines reduced fares.
2. More people can afford to fly abroad.
**Answer:** Cheaper travel.
## More detail
### Factors affecting the growth of tourism
- **Economic**: rising incomes, exchange rates, low-cost airlines.
- **Social**: more leisure time, ageing population with savings, social media.
- **Technological**: online booking, mobile apps, larger aircraft.
- **Political**: visa rules, stability, trade agreements.
### Factors causing a fall in tourism
- Natural disasters (tsunami 2004), pandemics (COVID-19), terrorism, political unrest, recession, rising fuel prices.
### Key data skills
- Percentage change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100.
- Read graphs carefully: give figures with units and years.
### Tourism in the Maldives
- Main markets include China, India, Russia, the UK, Italy and Germany.
- The number of guesthouses on local islands has grown quickly, giving budget options.
### Exam-style question
**Q: Explain how changes in exchange rates can affect inbound tourism. (3)** If the local currency is weak, the destination becomes cheaper for foreign visitors, so arrivals may rise.
## Common mistakes
- Not developing the reason.
## Exam tips
- Use point, explain, example.
notes.Destination appeal:
## Overview
Destinations attract visitors through natural and built attractions, climate, culture and access.
## Key ideas
- Natural attractions (beaches, reefs), built attractions, events, culture.
- Accessibility: airports, seaplanes, visas.
- Accommodation and activities.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Attraction | Feature that draws visitors |
| Accessibility | How easy it is to reach a destination |
## Formulas and facts
- The Maldives' appeal: coral reefs, white sand beaches, luxury resorts, warm climate.
## Worked example
**Give two natural attractions of the Maldives.**
**Answer:** Coral reefs; sandy beaches.
## More detail
### Appeal factors
- **Natural attractions**: beaches, reefs, marine life (mantas, whale sharks), lagoons, climate.
- **Built attractions**: museums, mosques (Old Friday Mosque), theme parks, shopping areas.
- **Cultural attractions**: food, music (bodu beru), festivals, handicrafts (lacquer work).
- **Events**: sports competitions, festivals, conferences.
- **Accessibility**: flight connections, visas, seaplanes and domestic flights.
- **Accommodation**: range from guesthouses to luxury resorts.
- **Safety and image**: low crime, political stability, positive reviews.
### Why appeal changes
- Overcrowding, pollution, natural disasters, new competitors, changing fashions.
### Exam-style question
**Q: Explain why the Maldives appeals to honeymoon couples. (4)** Privacy on one-island-one-resort; luxury overwater villas; romantic dining on the beach; warm climate all year.
## Common mistakes
- Listing built features as natural.
## Exam tips
- Use local examples.
notes.Managing destinations:
## Overview
Destinations must be planned and managed to stay successful.
## Key ideas
- Destination life cycle (Butler): exploration, involvement, development, consolidation, stagnation, decline or rejuvenation.
- Management: zoning, visitor limits, planning rules, education.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Zoning | Areas set aside for different uses |
| Rejuvenation | Renewing a destination's appeal |
## Formulas and facts
- Stakeholders: government, local people, businesses, tourists.
## Worked example
**How can zoning protect a reef?**
**Answer:** Some areas are closed to boats and divers so the reef can recover.
## More detail
### Visitor management techniques
- **Hard techniques**: fences, permits, timed entry, closing areas, parking limits.
- **Soft techniques**: education, signs, codes of conduct, guided tours, promoting other places.
- **Zoning**: separating activities (diving area, fishing area, protected zone).
- **Pricing**: higher fees in peak times to spread demand.
### Destination management organisations (DMOs)
- Plan development, set standards, market the destination, collect data, coordinate businesses.
- In the Maldives: Ministry of Tourism, Visit Maldives (Maldives Marketing and PR Corporation).
### Carrying capacity
- **Physical**: number of people the space can hold. **Environmental**: before damage occurs. **Perceptual**: before visitors feel it is too crowded.
### Exam-style question
**Q: Explain two ways to reduce damage at a popular dive site. (4)** Limit dive numbers per day with permits; require divers to attend a reef briefing and use mooring buoys instead of anchors.
## Common mistakes
- Not naming the stage of the life cycle.
## Exam tips
- Link management methods to specific problems.
notes.Impacts of tourism:
## Overview
Tourism has positive and negative economic, social and environmental impacts.
## Key ideas
- Economic: jobs, income, multiplier effect vs leakage, seasonal jobs.
- Social: cultural exchange vs loss of traditions, crime, crowding.
- Environmental: conservation funding vs pollution, reef damage, waste.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Multiplier effect | Tourist spending creates further spending |
| Leakage | Money that leaves the local economy |
| Demonstration effect | Locals copy tourists' behaviour |
## Formulas and facts
- Imported food and foreign staff increase leakage.
## Worked example
**Explain one negative environmental impact of tourism.**
1. Boats and divers damage coral.
2. Reef ecosystems decline.
**Answer:** Coral reef damage.
## More detail
### Economic
- **Positive**: jobs (direct, indirect, induced), foreign currency, tax (T-GST, green tax), infrastructure, multiplier effect.
- **Negative**: leakage (imported goods, foreign staff and owners), seasonal employment, inflation, over-dependence.
### Socio-cultural
- **Positive**: cultural exchange, pride, revival of crafts and traditions, better local services.
- **Negative**: commodification of culture, conflicts over dress and alcohol, crime, demonstration effect (locals copying tourists).
### Environmental
- **Positive**: conservation funding, awareness, cleaned-up areas, protected areas.
- **Negative**: reef damage, beach erosion, waste (Thilafushi), water shortages, carbon emissions from flights, noise.
### Reducing negative impacts
- Train and employ locals, buy local, educate tourists, limit numbers, waste recycling, renewable energy.
### Exam-style question
**Q: Discuss whether tourism benefits local islands in the Maldives. (6)** Benefits: guesthouse income, jobs, better ferries and services. Costs: cultural conflicts, waste, rising land prices. Conclude with how local control can maximise benefits.
## Common mistakes
- Not saying whether the impact is positive or negative.
## Exam tips
- Balance positives and negatives in evaluations.
notes.Tourism organisations:
## Overview
Public and private organisations work together in travel and tourism.
## Key ideas
- Public sector: tourism ministry, tourist boards (e.g. Visit Maldives) for promotion and regulation.
- Private sector: tour operators, travel agents, hotels, airlines.
- Integration: horizontal and vertical.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Tour operator | Puts together package holidays |
| Travel agent | Sells travel products to customers |
| Vertical integration | Joining firms at different levels of the chain |
## Formulas and facts
- Package = transport + accommodation + other services.
## Worked example
**Give one role of a national tourist board.**
**Answer:** Promoting the country abroad.
## More detail
### Sectors
| Sector | Aim | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Public | Serve the public, regulate, promote | Ministry of Tourism, Visit Maldives |
| Private | Make a profit | Resorts, airlines, tour operators |
| Voluntary | Not-for-profit, a cause | Environmental charities, reef-protection groups |
### Roles
- **Tour operator**: buys components in bulk and sells package holidays.
- **Travel agent**: retails travel products and gives advice; earns commission.
- **Online travel agents (OTAs)**: Booking.com, Expedia.
- **Tourist information centre**: free information, maps, bookings.
### Chain of distribution
- Principals (hotels, airlines) → tour operators (wholesalers) → travel agents (retailers) → customers.
- **Integration**: horizontal (two companies at the same level merge); vertical (companies at different levels join).
- **Disintermediation**: customers book directly online, cutting out agents.
### Package holidays
- Advantages: convenient, one price, often cheaper, support from a rep. Disadvantages: less flexibility, may be crowded.
## Common mistakes
- Mixing up tour operators and travel agents.
## Exam tips
- Give public and private examples.
notes.Transport & infrastructure:
## Overview
Transport and infrastructure make destinations accessible.
## Key ideas
- Air (international and seaplanes), sea (speedboats, ferries, cruise), land.
- Infrastructure: airports, harbours, roads, utilities.
- Choosing transport: cost, speed, comfort, convenience.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Infrastructure | Basic systems and structures a destination needs |
| Hub airport | Airport used for connecting flights |
## Formulas and facts
- Velana International Airport is the main gateway to the Maldives.
## Worked example
**Why do resorts far from Malé use seaplanes?**
**Answer:** They are fast over long sea distances and give scenic views.
## More detail
### Transport in the Maldives
- **Velana International Airport**: main gateway; new terminal increases capacity.
- **Seaplanes**: fast, scenic, but only daylight and weather dependent.
- **Domestic flights**: reach distant atolls; then speedboat transfer.
- **Speedboats and ferries**: cheaper for nearby islands; public ferries for guesthouse tourists.
### Comparing modes
| Mode | Advantages | Disadvantages |
|---|---|---|
| Air | Fast, long distance | Expensive, emissions |
| Sea (ferry, speedboat) | Cheaper, flexible | Slower, weather |
| Cruise | Many destinations | Overcrowding at ports |
| Road | Door-to-door | Congestion in Malé |
### Infrastructure
- Airports, seaports and jetties, roads, water supply (desalination), electricity, sewage and waste disposal, telecommunications, hospitals.
- **Superstructure**: tourist-specific facilities (hotels, restaurants, attractions).
### Exam-style question
**Q: Explain why improved infrastructure is important for guesthouse tourism. (4)** Visitors need reliable transfers, clean water, power and Wi-Fi; without them, satisfaction and reviews fall.
## Common mistakes
- Not comparing alternatives.
## Exam tips
- Explain advantages for specific customers.
notes.Customer service:
## Overview
Good customer service creates satisfied, loyal customers.
## Key ideas
- Meet and exceed expectations; handle complaints; communicate clearly.
- Staff skills: product knowledge, body language, listening.
- Benefits: repeat business, good reviews, higher sales.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Customer satisfaction | Customer needs and expectations are met |
| Complaint handling | Resolving problems professionally |
## Formulas and facts
- Steps for complaints: listen, apologise, find a solution, follow up.
## Worked example
**Describe how to handle a guest's complaint about a noisy room.**
1. Listen and apologise.
2. Offer a quieter room.
3. Follow up later.
**Answer:** Listen, solve, follow up.
## More detail
### Meeting customer needs
- Information and advice, assistance, special requests (dietary needs, celebrations), accessibility, safety and security.
- **Moments of truth**: each contact point (booking, arrival, check-in, departure) shapes the customer's view.
### Staff skills
- Clear verbal and written communication, positive body language, active listening, product knowledge, language skills, teamwork, problem-solving.
- Presentation: uniform, grooming, punctuality.
### Measuring service
- Feedback forms, online reviews (TripAdvisor), mystery shoppers, repeat bookings, complaints records.
### Benefits of excellent service
| To the customer | To the business | To staff |
|---|---|---|
| Satisfied, safe, valued | Loyalty, good reviews, more sales, better reputation | Job satisfaction, motivation, tips |
### Exam-style question
**Q: Explain two ways a resort could measure customer satisfaction. (4)** Ask guests to fill in a feedback form at check-out; monitor online review scores and comments over time.
## Common mistakes
- Blaming the customer.
## Exam tips
- Link service to business success.
notes.Marketing mix:
## Overview
The marketing mix (4Ps) helps tourism businesses sell their products.
## Key ideas
- Product (tangible and intangible), price (premium, discount, seasonal), place (distribution, online booking), promotion (social media, brochures, fam trips).
- Product life cycle and branding.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Familiarisation trip | Free trip for agents or journalists to promote a destination |
| Seasonal pricing | Higher prices in peak season |
## Formulas and facts
- Online travel agents widen distribution.
## Worked example
**Why do resorts use seasonal pricing?**
**Answer:** To maximise revenue in peak season and attract guests in low season.
## More detail
### Product
- Tangible (rooms, food) and intangible (experience, service) features. Branding, USP, packaging of services.
- **Product life cycle**: introduction, growth, maturity, decline; extension by new activities or refurbishment.
### Price
| Strategy | When used |
|---|---|
| Penetration | Enter a new market with low prices |
| Skimming | High price for a new, unique product |
| Premium | Luxury brands (overwater villas) |
| Competitive | Match rivals |
| Promotional / discount | Fill rooms in low season |
| Variable / seasonal | Higher in peak season |
| Bundle | Package of room + meals + activities |
### Place
- Direct sales (own website), indirect (travel agents, OTAs, tour operators), social media booking.
### Promotion
- Advertising, brochures, websites, social media and influencers, sales promotions, PR, familiarisation (fam) trips, travel fairs (ITB Berlin).
- **AIDA**: Attention, Interest, Desire, Action.
### Exam-style question
**Q: Explain why a resort might use seasonal pricing. (3)** Demand is higher in peak season, so higher prices raise revenue; lower prices in low season attract more guests.
## Common mistakes
- Describing only one P when the mix is asked.
## Exam tips
- Link each P to the target market.
notes.Market research & segmentation:
## Overview
Market research finds out what customers want; segmentation groups them.
## Key ideas
- Primary research: surveys, interviews, observation, feedback forms.
- Secondary research: statistics, reports, websites.
- Segmentation: age, income, lifestyle, nationality, purpose of travel.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Target market | Group a product is aimed at |
| Qualitative data | Opinions and feelings |
| Quantitative data | Numbers and statistics |
## Formulas and facts
- SWOT analysis: strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats.
## Worked example
**Give one advantage of online guest surveys.**
**Answer:** Cheap and reach many guests quickly.
## More detail
### Research methods
| Primary | Secondary |
|---|---|
| Questionnaires, interviews, focus groups, observation, guest feedback | Government statistics, industry reports, competitor websites, online reviews |
| Specific and up to date | Cheap and quick |
| Costly and time-consuming | May be out of date or general |
- **Quantitative** (numbers) vs **qualitative** (opinions and reasons).
### Segmentation
- **Demographic**: age, gender, income, family stage.
- **Geographic**: country or region of origin.
- **Psychographic**: lifestyle, values, interests (adventure, wellness).
- **Behavioural**: spending, loyalty, purpose of trip.
### SWOT and PEST
- **SWOT**: Strengths, Weaknesses (internal); Opportunities, Threats (external).
- **PEST**: Political, Economic, Social, Technological factors.
### Exam-style question
**Q: Suggest two questions for a guest survey and explain their purpose. (4)** "How did you hear about us?" shows which promotion works; "Rate our food from 1 to 5" measures satisfaction.
## Common mistakes
- Mixing up primary and secondary research.
## Exam tips
- Give advantages and disadvantages of each method.

l.t: Types of tourism and reasons to travel
l.md:
## In short
Tourism is travelling away from home for at least one night for leisure, business or to visit friends and relatives.
## Learn it
### Types of tourism
- **Domestic:** within your own country (Malé to Addu).
- **Inbound:** visitors coming into a country (tourists arriving in the Maldives).
- **Outbound:** residents travelling abroad.
### Reasons to travel
- **Leisure:** holidays, sport, culture, health and wellness.
- **Business:** meetings, conferences, exhibitions (MICE).
- **VFR:** visiting friends and relatives.
- Others: religion (Hajj), education, medical.
### Types of travel
- Independent travel vs **package holidays**; short breaks; long-haul and short-haul.
## Remember
- Use the Maldives as an example of an inbound destination.

## In short
Tourism has grown fast because of changes in transport, technology, income and society.
## Learn it
- Cheaper flights (low-cost airlines), more disposable income, paid holidays, more leisure time.
- **Technology:** online booking, mobile apps, social media.
- Changing tastes: adventure, eco-tourism, wellness.
- Factors that reduce tourism: natural disasters, pandemics, terrorism, economic recession.
## Remember
- Link each factor to how it increases demand.

## In short
The industry is made of many sectors that work together.
## Learn it
| Sector | Examples |
|---|---|
| Accommodation | Resorts, guest houses, liveaboards |
| Transport | Airlines, seaplanes, speedboats |
| Tour operators | Make package holidays |
| Travel agents | Sell holidays to customers |
| Attractions | Dive sites, museums, theme parks |
| Tourist information | Visit Maldives |
- **Public sector:** government, tourism boards. **Private sector:** businesses for profit. **Voluntary sector:** charities.
- **Chain of distribution:** principals → tour operators → travel agents → customers.
- **Integration:** horizontal (same level) and vertical (different levels).
## Remember
- Liveaboards combine transport and accommodation.

## In short
Tourism brings income and jobs but can also bring economic problems.
## Learn it
### Positive
- Jobs (direct and indirect), foreign currency, tax income, better infrastructure, **multiplier effect**.
### Negative
- **Leakage:** money leaving the country (imported food, foreign owners).
- Seasonal jobs, low wages, over-dependence on tourism, inflation.
## Remember
- Leakage is high in the Maldives because most goods are imported.

## In short
Tourism affects local people and the natural environment.
## Learn it
### Socio-cultural
- Positive: pride in culture, new facilities, cultural exchange.
- Negative: loss of culture, crime, overcrowding, behaviour that offends local customs.
### Environmental
- Positive: money for conservation, protected areas (e.g. Baa Atoll UNESCO Biosphere Reserve).
- Negative: coral damage, pollution, waste, water shortages, erosion.
## Remember
- In answers, give a specific example and explain the effect.

## In short
Sustainable tourism meets the needs of tourists today without harming the future.
## Learn it
- Three parts: **economic, social, environmental** sustainability.
- Methods: limiting visitor numbers, eco-resorts, solar power, banning single-use plastics, marine protected areas, using local products and staff, education of tourists.
- **Responsible tourism:** tourists respect culture and nature.
- **Carrying capacity:** the maximum number of visitors a place can take without damage.
## Remember
- Mention local community involvement.

## In short
Destinations attract visitors because of their natural, built and cultural features.
## Learn it
- **Natural:** beaches, reefs, climate, wildlife.
- **Built:** hotels, attractions, infrastructure.
- **Cultural:** food, music (bodu beru), festivals, history.
- **Accessibility:** flights, visa rules, distance.
- **Image and safety.**
- **Types of destination:** coastal, rural, urban, mountain, purpose-built.
## Remember
- Use climate graphs and maps carefully in data questions.

## In short
Destinations must be planned and managed to stay attractive and sustainable.
## Learn it
- **Destination management organisations** (DMOs) plan and promote.
- Tools: zoning, visitor management, infrastructure planning, regulations, education.
- **Tourism Area Life Cycle (Butler):** exploration, involvement, development, consolidation, stagnation, decline or rejuvenation.
## Remember
- Recognise each life-cycle stage from data (visitor numbers, facilities).

## In short
Excellent customer service makes customers happy, loyal and likely to recommend the business.
## Learn it
- Skills: communication, product knowledge, problem solving, teamwork, positive attitude, presentation.
- **Internal customers** (colleagues) and **external customers** (guests).
- Customers with **specific needs:** families, disabled guests, different languages, business travellers.
- Benefits: repeat business, good reviews, competitive advantage.
## Remember
- Complaint handling: listen, apologise, solve, follow up.

## In short
Businesses measure service quality to improve it.
## Learn it
- Questionnaires, online reviews (TripAdvisor), mystery shoppers, comment cards, focus groups.
- **Service standards** set clear expectations (e.g. answer calls within 3 rings).
## Remember
- Use measurement results to train staff and improve.

## In short
Products include transport, accommodation, attractions and ancillary services.
## Learn it
- **Accommodation grading** (stars). Board types: room only, B&B, half board, full board, all-inclusive.
- **Transport:** air, sea, land; scheduled and charter flights.
- **Ancillary services:** travel insurance, car hire, currency exchange, visas.
- **Package holiday:** transport + accommodation (+ extras) sold as one product.
- **Dynamic packaging:** customers build their own package online.
## Remember
- Compare products for a specific customer type in exam answers.

## In short
Marketing uses the 4 Ps to reach the right customers.
## Learn it
- **Product:** features, branding, product life cycle.
- **Price:** penetration, skimming, promotional, discount, variable/seasonal pricing.
- **Place:** distribution channels, direct booking online.
- **Promotion:** advertising, social media influencers, brochures, familiarisation trips, trade fairs.
## Remember
- Seasonal pricing is common: high prices in peak season (December–April).

## In short
Businesses research their market and divide customers into segments.
## Learn it
- **Primary research:** surveys, interviews, observation. **Secondary:** reports, statistics.
- **Segmentation:** age, income, lifestyle, nationality, purpose of travel.
- **SWOT** and **PEST** analysis help plan marketing.
## Remember
- Match the promotion method to the target segment.
